findings.detail: Both words in the shipped gloss name the wrong action to any learner. 'translate' is the archaic theological sense (as in 'Enoch was translated to heaven'), and a German learner will read it as übersetzen — the single most confusable false lead possible in a language app. 'rapture' as a transitive verb is not ordinary English either. The verb means to carry someone off to another place or state, and in living use it is the mental/spiritual sense: die Musik entrückte ihn, and the participle entrückt 'rapt, in a trance, far away'. candidate_glosses has this at index 1 ('to ravish, to enrapture, to enthrall (spiritually)') and index 2 ('to transport, to carry away (mentally)'); the importer took index 0.

'relieve' standing alone reads in English as relieve pain or relieve pressure, which is erleichtern or lindern, not entheben. Entheben takes a genitive of the thing someone is freed from and its live use is jemanden seines Amtes entheben — remove from office, relieve of duty (hence Amtsenthebung). The gloss points at the right action but the one word most learners will resolve it to is the wrong verb.

Correct as far as it goes, but leading with 'fall asleep' invites the error the verb is most likely to cause: a learner glossing entschlafen onto einschlafen and writing ich bin gestern früh entschlafen. Modern entschlafen is a euphemism for dying (sanft entschlafen, die Entschlafenen) and is not used for ordinary sleep. Putting 'die' second, after a comma the house style reads as 'these mean the same thing', understates that the death sense is the only one in use.
